errata.text: Break-even is attributed to the wrong selector. README "DERIVED EXTRAPOLATION" (Break-even bullet) says "a selection costing even one Legendre-only frame enumeration (the 0.1 GAE column) pays only if the index-calculus attack itself costs at least 2.8·10²¹ × rho", and Answer 4 says "Selection could only pay for an index-calculus attack that is already more than about 2.8·10²¹ × rho". 2.79·10²¹ is C_sel·(1 + 1/e) with C_sel = the FULL-LABEL enumeration (1,141.9 × rho, analyse.py takes the minimum of full_label_over_rho over w), e = 4.086·10⁻¹⁹. For the Legendre-only (one-bit / c-only) selector, which captures 96–100% of the excess, the break-even is 1.66·10¹⁸ × rho at 0.1 GAE and 1.66·10¹⁹ × rho at 1 GAE, and at w = 0 it costs no group operations. The same text is in REPORT.typ/PDF.
errata.suggested_fix: Break-even: full-label selection (1,142 × rho per frame) pays only if the IC attack costs at least 2.8·10²¹ × rho; a Legendre-only selection pays only above 1.7·10¹⁸ × rho (0.1 GAE) or 1.7·10¹⁹ × rho (1 GAE), and at w = 0 it costs no group operations but its gain is 1 + 4·10⁻¹⁹. Answer 4: replace the single 2.8·10²¹ bound by these three figures. Record in the README Errata section; leave analysis/results.json byte-equal.

errata.text: README "Sampling instead of enumerating": "about 2^126.8 samples per frame ... That is more than the frame's 2^127 columns". 2^126.77 is 0.85 × 2^127, fewer than the columns, not more; the 974 × rho sampled cost against 1,142 × rho enumerated is that 0.85 ratio.
errata.suggested_fix: "about 2^126.8 samples per frame, 0.85 × the frame's 2^127 columns, so sampling saves at most about 15% (974 vs 1,142 × rho per frame with full labels)."

errata.text: README "Selection cost": "Arm R used about 9.9·10⁶ Legendre symbols for on-curve tests, plus one more per label for the parity check". On-curve tests total 9,509,937 (R1 793,600; R1c 8,192,000; R2 524,337 trials). 9,907,318 is the sum of the R1 "legendre" fields, which already include 397,381 parity symbols, plus R1c and the R2 trials; it omits R2's 262,144 parity symbols.
errata.suggested_fix: "about 9.51·10⁶ Legendre symbols for on-curve tests plus 659,525 for the parity check (1.017·10⁷ in total)."

errata.text: README "Selection cost": "A double-and-add count for r would be 324 ops (251 doublings, 73 additions)". r has 253 bits and popcount 73, so double-and-add is 252 doublings and 72 additions; the total 324 is right.

Disclosures, smoke vs data seeds: "Curve25519 R2: the data frames differ from the smoke frames; only frame 0's start point coincides." The smoke R2 (K = 8, n = 64, same derived seed) frame 0 shares more than its start point: its 64 labelled samples and their trials are the first 64 samples of data frame 0. The validator regenerated both and they are equal. This is 64 of 262,144 samples. Without frame 0 the R2/R3 verdicts still hold (p = 0.450, 0.269, 0.0109; R3 inside).
errata.suggested_fix: "R2: data frame 0 starts at the smoke frame 0 point and its first 64 labelled samples are the smoke samples; the other 63 data frames differ. R2/R3 recomputed without frame 0 still hold."

errata.text: Result sentences without [pcc:unverified]: Answer item 4 (all five bullets, README lines 31–36) and the DERIVED EXTRAPOLATION bullets (t*, excess at t*, rho, the cost table, sampling, isogeny-tower note) carry no tag. Only the break-even bullet does. The brief requires every result sentence to carry it. "At 255 bits the selector is worthless" is also an interpretive dismissal (AGENTS.md "Preserve scope and report evidence").
errata.suggested_fix: Tag each derived bullet [pcc:unverified] (as well as DERIVED) and replace "worthless" with the quantitative statement, e.g. "At 255 bits the derived selector excess is about 4·10⁻¹⁹ (DERIVED EXTRAPOLATION) [pcc:unverified]".

errata.text: Answer 1, "The gain dies like 2^(−t/2)", is stated without its caveat. M3 wins the held-out test because the preregistered rule prefers the simpler model. But the free-α (M2) 95% intervals exclude 0.5 on k24f [0.530, 0.579] and k24r [0.514, 0.588]; k20 is [0.501, 0.618]. Unweighted fits give α 0.59, and under unweighted LS the seed arm's winner becomes M2 (worst 0.092 vs 0.223). Separately, "M1 ... predicts gain < 1 on the held-out t" holds for frames and k24r seeds but not for k20 seeds, where M1 scores a finite 1.427 (still inadequate).
errata.suggested_fix: "Under the preregistered rule the one-parameter 2^(−t/2) form (M3) wins on every curve; the free exponent fits 0.55–0.59 and its intervals exclude 0.5 on k24f and k24r. M3 is the conservative (larger-excess) extrapolation; M2 gives 2–5·10⁻²¹ at t*." Qualify the M1 sentence for k20 seeds.

errata.text: The P5 band only applies to one counting rule. The preregistered rule is the counted double-and-add (20/27/25 ops = 1.18/1.29/1.19 log2 r, fixed by r's bit length and popcount). Under that rule P5 holds as worded. An x-only ladder count (two ops per bit of r) gives 36/44/44 = 2.12/2.10/2.10 log2 r, outside 1.0–1.6. Yet the 255-bit per-label cost uses the ladder count (506 = 2.01 log2 r). With the double-and-add count (324), full-label enumeration at t* would cost 731 × rho, not 1,142 × rho. The README P5 row reads "[r]P costs 1.0–1.6·log₂ r" without naming the counting rule.
errata.suggested_fix: Name the counting rule in the P5 row ("counted double-and-add"). Give both 255-bit full-label figures (ladder 1,142 × rho; double-and-add 731 × rho), labelled derived.
